info.title: Grepvine API
info.description: Control-plane and search API for the Grepvine beta.

tags.name: Device login
tags.description: Device authorization for the command-line client.

tags.name: Connections
tags.description: Apps connected to an account through OAuth sign-in, such as MCP clients.

post.description: A 409 has code `username_taken` when an account or an organization already holds the username, and code `email_taken` when an account already uses the email address. A 403 has code `invitation_required` when registration is by invitation and the request carries none, and code `invitation_invalid` when the invitation it carries was already used, was withdrawn or has expired. A valid invitation is accepted with the registration, and the account joins the organization it names, if any.

201.description: The user and session were created.

get.description: How accounts are created on this service. The console reads it to decide whether to offer registration without an invitation.

post.description: Reports what a pending invitation offers, so the registration form can show it. The token travels in the body, never in the URL. An invitation that was used, withdrawn or has expired is not found.

get.summary: Check whether a username is available
get.description: Reports whether an account can register this username now. Accounts and organizations share one namespace, so a name either one holds, in any case, is taken. The answer can change before the name is registered.

200.description: Whether an account can register this username now. Accounts and organizations share one namespace. The answer can change before the name is registered.

post.description: Signs in with a username or email address and a password, and starts a browser session: the response sets the session cookie and returns, in X-Csrf-Token, the token every state change made with that cookie must send. A 401 means the credentials were not accepted. Programs authenticate with an API key instead.
Ends the session that made the request and clears its cookie. Other sessions and API keys are unaffected.

get.description: Returns the account the request authenticates as, whether with a session or an API key. A session request also receives its CSRF token in X-Csrf-Token.

put.description: Changes the signed-in account's password after checking the current one. Every other session of the account is signed out; the session that made the request stays signed in, and API keys keep working. A 401 means the current password was wrong.

post.description: Starts signing in a device, such as the command-line client, without entering a password on it. Show the user `user_code` and send them to `verification_uri` (or `verification_uri_complete`) to approve it in a signed-in browser, then poll for the API key with `device_code`. The authorization expires after `expires_in` seconds.
Returns the scope a pending device authorization asks for. Only a signed-in session can read one.

Approves a pending device authorization, identified by the code the device shows. The device's next poll receives a new API key with the name it asked for. Without a scope it grants what the device asked for; a scope replaces that as a whole, narrower or wider. The key never does more than the approving account can. A code that is unknown, already decided or expired is not found. Only a signed-in session can approve.

Denies a pending device authorization, identified by the code the device shows. The device's next poll fails with code `access_denied`. A code that is unknown, already decided or expired is not found.

post.summary: Poll for a device API key
post.description: Exchanges an approved device code for an API key, once. Until the user decides, a poll fails with 400 and code `authorization_pending`: poll again after `interval` seconds. Polling sooner fails with `slow_down` and adds 5 seconds to the interval. A denied authorization fails with `access_denied`, and an unknown, expired or already used code with `expired_token`.

200.description: The device API key. The key is shown once.

post.description: Returns who an app signing in through OAuth is and what it asks to do, for a signed-in session to show before approving it. The permissions are those the request's `scope` names that an app can be granted; without any, `search` and `read`. A request that cannot be approved fails with 400, and its app is not sent back an answer. Only a signed-in session can read one.

200.description: The app and what it asks for.

post.description: Approves an app's sign-in request with the scope the signed-in account chose, creating a connection, and returns the address to send the browser to, which hands the app a single-use code. The connection never does more than the approving account can, and expires after 90 days unless the app keeps using it. `manage_members` and `manage_organization` cannot be granted to an app. A 404 means the organization or an index named does not exist or is not visible. Only a signed-in session can approve.
Denies an app's sign-in request and returns the address to send the browser to, which tells the app it was refused with `access_denied`. Only a signed-in session can deny.

get.description: Lists the apps you have connected that are still in use: revoked and ended connections are left out. Newest first. Only a signed-in session can list them.

delete.description: Revokes one of the authenticated account's connections. The app's requests are refused from then on, and it must sign in again. A connection that doesn't exist, is already revoked or belongs to another account is not found. Only a signed-in session can revoke one.

get.description: Lists the authenticated account's API keys, oldest first, including revoked ones. The secret key itself is never returned again; `prefix` tells keys apart.

post.description: Creates a key that reaches one organization or all of the account's, a list of indexes or all of them, with a set of permissions, until it expires. A 404 means the organization or an index named does not exist or is not visible. Only a signed-in session can create, list or revoke keys. The response is the only time the secret key is shown, so store it securely. Send it as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

201.description: The new API key. The key is shown once.

delete.description: Revokes one of the authenticated account's API keys. Requests authenticated with it are refused from then on. A key that doesn't exist or belongs to another account is not found.

get.description: Lists the organizations the authenticated account belongs to, with its role in each, ordered by name.

post.description: Creates an organization owned by the authenticated account. Accounts and organizations share one namespace, so a 409 means an account or organization already holds the name, in any case.

get.description: Returns an organization the authenticated account belongs to, with its role there. It answers for a suspended organization too, and reports `suspended`.

delete.description: Starts deleting an organization with all its indexes and documents. Only the owner can delete it. The deletion finishes in the background and can't be undone.

get.description: Lists an organization's members and their roles, ordered by name. Requires the owner or admin role.

post.description: Adds an existing account to the organization with the admin, developer or reader role. Requires the owner or admin role. An organization has one owner, changed only by transferring ownership.

put.description: Changes a member's role to admin, developer or reader. Requires the owner or admin role. The owner's role changes only by transferring ownership.

delete.description: Removes a member from the organization. Requires the owner or admin role. The owner can't be removed; transfer ownership first.

put.description: Makes another member the owner. Only the owner can transfer ownership, and the previous owner stays a member with the admin role. The new owner must already be a member, and not one with time-limited access.

get.description: Lists the organization's indexes, ordered by name. Any member can list them.

200.description: A page of indexes, ordered by name. Document counts, sizes and last write times can trail the most recent writes by a few seconds; read one index for its current values.

post.description: Creates an empty index. Requires the owner or admin role. A new index is usually `ready` in the response; if it is still `creating`, read it until it is `ready`. A 409 means the organization already has an index with that name, in any case.

get.description: Returns one index with its current state, document count and size, and the progress of its background optimization while one runs. Any member can read it.

patch.description: Changes the index's description or tags. A field absent from the request is left as it is. The name is immutable.

delete.description: Starts deleting an index and all its documents. Requires the owner or admin role. The index is `deleting` until the deletion finishes in the background, and it can't be undone.

get.description: Lists documents in key byte order, with each one's revision, size, metadata and whether a search can match it. Narrow the listing with `prefix`, and add `delimiter` to browse keys like a directory tree: keys that share the part up to the next delimiter are returned once, in `common_prefixes`.

200.description: A page of documents and folded common prefixes.

put.description:
Stores one document of at most 1 GiB. Content that is valid UTF-8 and at most 100 MiB is
searchable. Any other content, such as an image or a larger file, is stored, listed, and served
by the document endpoints but is never matched by a search. The `searchable` field of a listing
reports which applies.

get.description: Returns a document's content exactly as it was stored, its revision in the ETag header and its metadata in the X-Grepvine-Metadata header. Send a Range header to read one byte range; the response is then 206, or 416 when the range lies outside the document.

416.description: The byte range does not overlap the document.

delete.description: Deletes one document. Send If-Match with a revision to delete it only if it still has that revision. Retrying with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original result. Once acknowledged, the document no longer matches any search.

post.description:
Stores up to 2,048 documents. Each document is stored on its own: a document whose precondition
fails is not stored, the others are, and the result of each document says which happened. Retrying
with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same results and stores any document an interrupted
attempt did not reach. Batch content is text carried as JSON strings, so every document stored this
way is searchable. Store binary content, or a document over 16 MiB, with the
single-document endpoint. The body may be sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip`; the service decodes it
before applying the limits below, and answers any other content encoding with 415
`unsupported_content_encoding`.

schema.description: One PutObjectRecord JSON value per line; at most 2,048 records and 16 MiB of combined object content.

200.description: The batch was applied. Each result reports one document, in request order.

post.description:
Deletes up to 2,048 documents. Each document is deleted on its own: a document that does not
exist or whose precondition fails is not deleted, the others are, and the result of each document
says which happened. Retrying with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same results.

200.description: The batch was applied. Each result reports one document, in request order.

post.description: Searches every searchable document in the index for a regular expression or literal text, and returns each match with the lines it covers, sorted by key, then line, then offset. A metadata filter restricts the search to matching documents, and context lines can be returned around each result. A pattern or filter that doesn't parse is rejected with 400 and code `invalid_pattern` or `invalid_filter`. Continue with `page` while `has_next` is true: a page can be empty while more results follow.

200.description: A page of results. Each result is one match, or several matches that share lines, together with the lines it covers.

AcceptRanges.description: The range unit accepted for document reads.

ContentLength.description: The number of content bytes in this response.

ContentRange.description: The returned range and complete document size, or the complete size for an unsatisfied range.

DocumentMetadata.description: The document TaggedMetadata object encoded as JSON.

CSRFToken.description: The token for state changes that use cookie authentication.

SessionCookie.description: The secure opaque session cookie, or an expired cookie when the session is cleared.

RequestID.description: The request identifier used for support and audit correlation.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with every 429 so a client slows down instead of failing.

Amount.description: The largest number of results to return in one page, from 1 to 200. Defaults to 50. A page can hold fewer, even none, while more follow.
Amount.name: amount

Page.description: The `next_page_id` of the previous page, to continue where it stopped; omit it for the first page. A token is valid for 15 minutes, and only for the same caller and the same request, including `amount`.
Page.name: page

Organization.description: The organization's name. Any spelling that differs only in case refers to the same organization.
Organization.name: organization

Index.description: The index's name within the organization. Any spelling that differs only in case refers to the same index.
Index.name: index

IndexPrefix.name: prefix
IndexPrefix.description: Lists only the indexes whose names start with this literal prefix, compared without regard to case. A page token is valid only with the prefix it was issued for.

DocumentKey.description: The document's key: a UTF-8, POSIX-style path of at most 1,024 bytes, with no empty, `.` or `..` components.
DocumentKey.name: key

Prefix.description: Lists only the documents whose keys start with this prefix, compared byte for byte. At most 1,024 characters.
Prefix.name: prefix

Delimiter.name: delimiter
Delimiter.description: Folds documents that share the substring through the first delimiter after prefix into one common prefix.

Range.name: Range
Range.description: One HTTP bytes range. Multiple ranges are not supported.

User.description: The member's account name. Any spelling that differs only in case refers to the same account.
User.name: user

APIKeyID.description: The ID of the API key, as the listing returns it.
APIKeyID.name: api_key_id

ConnectionID.description: The ID of the connection, as the listing returns it.
ConnectionID.name: connection_id

IdempotencyKey.description: A key of 16 to 128 characters that identifies this write. Keep it the same when you retry: repeating the request with the same key returns the original result and applies the write at most once.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

CSRFToken.name: X-Csrf-Token
CSRFToken.description: Required for a state change that uses cookie authentication.

IfMatch.description: A revision. The write applies only if the document still has this revision; otherwise the request fails with 412.
IfMatch.name: If-Match

IfNoneMatch.description: Set to `*` to store the document only if no document has this key yet; otherwise the request fails with 412.
IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match

Error.description: The request failed. A 429 carries Retry-After; the index is busy absorbing recent writes or is out of request capacity, and clients must slow down and retry after the interval. A 403 with code `organization_suspended` refuses every operation on a suspended organization's members, indexes, documents and searches; reading the organization itself still answers and reports `suspended`, and the client should contact support.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist or is not visible.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with current state.

Error.description: A failed request. `code` says what went wrong and is stable; branch on it, not on the message.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable code, such as `invalid_pattern`, `not_found` or `write_backlog`.

reason.description: The broad category of the error, such as `validation`, `authentication`, `state` or `capacity`.

error.description: A message for people that says what went wrong and what to do about it.

details.description: Structured information about the error. Omitted when there is none.

type.description: What the detail is, such as `missing_permission`.

Pagination.description: A page may hold fewer results than the requested amount, possibly none, while has_next is true; a query page stops at the server's soft time budget and next_page_id resumes exactly after the last candidate it examined. Clients continue while has_next is true.

next_page_id.description: The token for the next page: pass it as `page`. Empty when has_next is false.

has_next.description: Whether more results follow. Keep requesting pages until it is false, even after an empty page.

Name.description: An account or organization name. Accounts and organizations share one namespace. A name keeps the case it was created with, and any spelling that differs only in case refers to it; no other account or organization can take such a spelling.

IndexName.description: An index name, unique in its organization. A name keeps the case it was created with, and any spelling that differs only in case refers to it; no other index in the organization can take such a spelling.

staff_role.description: The account's role on the Grepvine team. Omitted for every other account.

StaffRole.description: The account's role on the Grepvine team, when it has one. Omitted for every other account.

name.description: The username. Accounts and organizations share one namespace.

email.description: The account's email address, at most 320 characters. No other account can use it.

invitation.description: The token of the invitation link the account was invited with. Required when registration is by invitation.

SignupMode.description: How accounts are created. `open` lets anyone register; `invite` registers only with an invitation.

AuthOptions.description: How accounts are created on this service.

signup.description: Whether anyone can register, or only with an invitation.

token.description: The token from the invitation link.

InvitationRole.description: The role an invitation grants in its organization.

email.description: The address the invitation was sent to, to prefill the registration form.

organization.description: The organization the account joins on registering. Omitted when the invitation names none.

role.description: The role the account receives in that organization.

UsernameAvailability.description: Whether a username can be registered.

available.description: Whether an account can register this username now.

identifier.description: A username or an email address, matched case-insensitively.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: The current password and its replacement.

DeviceAuthorizationRequest.description: Starts a device authorization. The scope fields are what the device asks for; the person approving it sees them and may change them. A scope field left out sets no limit.

api_key_name.description: The name to give the API key the device receives, 1 to 128 characters.

organization.description: The one organization the key reaches. Omitted for every organization of the account. A list of indexes needs one.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working, at most one year ahead. Omitted for a key that never expires.

PendingDeviceAuthorization.description: What a pending device authorization asks for.

api_key_name.description: The name the key the device receives will have.

organization.description: The one organization the device asks for. Omitted when it asks for every organization of the account.

expires_at.description: When the key the device receives stops working. Omitted when it never expires.

DeviceApprovalRequest.description: The device authorization to approve, and optionally the scope to grant.

user_code.description: The code the device shows. Hyphens, surrounding spaces and case are ignored.

scope.description: The scope to grant instead of the one the device asked for, as a whole. Without it, the device's request is approved as asked.

KeyScope.description: What a key reaches and may do. A field left out sets no limit.

organization.description: The one organization the key reaches. Omitted for every organization of the account. A list of indexes needs one.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working, at most one year ahead. Omitted for a key that never expires.

OAuthAuthorizationRequest.description: An app's OAuth sign-in request, with the parameters it sent to the authorization endpoint.

client_id.description: The app's client ID: the HTTPS address of its client metadata document.

redirect_uri.description: Where the app receives the answer; one of the addresses its metadata document lists.

code_challenge.description: The PKCE code challenge, 43 to 128 characters.

resource.description: The MCP server the app signs in to.

state.description: A value the app sent, returned to it unchanged, at most 1,024 characters.

scope.description: The space-separated scopes the app asked for.

PendingOAuthAuthorization.description: Who an app signing in is and what it asks for. The name is the app's own and is not verified; the host is where its metadata document is served.

client_name.description: The name the app gives itself.

client_host.description: The host that serves the app's client metadata document.

redirect_host.description: The host the answer is sent to.

loopback_redirect.description: Whether the answer is sent to this computer, as a desktop or command-line app receives it.

ConnectionScope.description: What a connection reaches and may do. A field left out sets no limit.

organization.description: The one organization the connection reaches. Omitted for every organization of the account. A list of indexes needs one.

OAuthApprovalRequest.description: The sign-in request to approve and the scope to grant it.

OAuthRedirect.description: Where to send the browser to answer the app.

redirect_to.description: The app's address, carrying the answer.

Connection.description: An app the account connected, and what it reaches and may do.

client_name.description: The name the app gave itself when it was connected.

client_host.description: The host that serves the app's client metadata document.

organization.description: The one organization the connection reaches. Omitted for every organization of the account.

last_used_at.description: When the app last signed in or renewed its access.

expires_at.description: When the connection stops working unless the app keeps using it.

DeviceAuthorization.description: A pending device sign-in: the codes to show the user and to poll with.

device_code.description: The secret code the device polls with. Keep it on the device; never show it.

user_code.description: The short code to show the user, who confirms it when approving.

verification_uri.description: The page where the user enters `user_code` and approves the device.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with `user_code` already filled in, for a link or QR code.

interval.description: The minimum number of seconds to wait between polls.

DeviceDecisionRequest.description: The device authorization to approve or deny.

user_code.description: The code the device shows. Hyphens, surrounding spaces and case are ignored.

DeviceTokenRequest.description: The device code to exchange for an API key.

Permission.description:
A permission a key can carry. A key never does more than its account's role allows in an organization.
`search` searches an index; `read` reads and lists its documents; `write` stores and deletes documents;
`create_index` creates indexes, and needs every index in scope; `manage_index` changes and deletes indexes.
`manage_members` adds members, changes their roles and removes them; `manage_organization` deletes the
organization. Both need a key scoped to one organization.

Permissions.description: The permissions a key carries, each named once.

IndexScope.description: The indexes a key reaches, by name, in the key's one organization. Omitted for every index of its organizations, including indexes created later. A request names at least one; a key's list is empty once every index it named is deleted.

CreateAPIKeyRequest.description: Creates an API key. A scope field left out sets no limit.

name.description: A name to tell the key apart, 1 to 128 characters.

organization.description: The one organization the key reaches. Omitted for every organization of the account. A list of indexes needs one.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working, at most one year ahead. Omitted for a key that never expires.

APIKey.description: An API key, without its secret.

name.description: The name the key was given.

prefix.description: The first characters of the key, shown to tell keys apart.

organization.description: The one organization the key reaches. Omitted when it reaches every organization of the account.

permissions.description: What the key may do. May be empty on a revoked key.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working. Omitted when it never expires.

last_used_at.description: When the key last authenticated a request. Omitted if it never has.

revoked_at.description: When the key was revoked. Omitted while the key is active.

APIKeyCreated.description: A new API key with its secret, which is shown only this once.

key.description: The secret API key. It is shown only in this response; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

results.description: The API keys on this page.

pagination.description: How to request the next page.

Organization.description: An organization, as seen by one of its members.

role.description: The authenticated account's role in the organization.

suspended.description: A suspended organization keeps its data, but refuses every operation on its members, indexes, documents and searches until it is resumed. Contact support.

pagination.description: How to request the next page.

name.description: The organization's name. Accounts and organizations share one namespace.

Role.description: A member's role in an organization. `owner` can do everything, including deleting the organization and transferring ownership; `admin` also manages members and indexes; `developer` reads, writes and searches documents; `reader` reads and searches them.

role.description: The member's role in the organization.

created_at.description: When the account became a member.

expires_at.description: When the membership ends, for time-limited access granted by Grepvine support. Omitted for an ordinary membership.

pagination.description: How to request the next page.

AddMemberRequest.description: The account to add and its role.

user.description: The username of the account to add.

role.description: The role to grant. `owner` is granted only by transferring ownership.
The new role. `owner` is granted only by transferring ownership.

TransferOwnershipRequest.description: The member who becomes the owner.

user.description: The username of the member who becomes the owner.

IndexState.description: Where an index is in its life. `creating`: not usable yet. `ready`: the only state that answers searches. `recreate_required`: answers nothing until it is deleted, created again and its documents written again. `deleting`: deletion is in progress. `delete_failed`: deletion did not finish and is retried.

IndexSummary.description: An index as a listing returns it.

organization.description: The name of the organization the index belongs to.

canonical_id.description: A stable identifier for the index, currently the same as `id`.

description.description: What the index holds, in Markdown. Empty when none was set.

tags.description: Key/value labels on the index. Empty when none was set.

state.description: Where the index is in its life. Only a `ready` index answers searches.

document_count.description: The number of documents in the index.

content_bytes.description: The total size of the documents' content, in bytes.

last_updated_at.description: When a document was last stored or deleted. Omitted when that is not known, such as before the first write.

Index.description: An index as a read of that one index returns it, which adds the progress of its background optimization.

permissions.description: What the caller may do with this index, among `search`, `read`, `write` and `manage_index`.

optimization_progress_percent.description: How far the background optimization of this index has progressed, as a percentage. Omitted when no optimization is running.

pagination.description: How to request the next page.

name.description: The index's name, unique in the organization regardless of case. It can't be changed later.

description.description: What the index holds, in Markdown, at most 16,384 characters. Optional.

tags.description: Key/value labels for the index, at most 64. Optional.

UpdateIndexRequest.description: The fields to change. A field that is absent is left as it is; at least one must be present.

description.description: The new description, which replaces the old one. An empty string clears it.

tags.description: Tags to set, by key, and tags to remove, given as null. Other tags are unchanged.

IndexDescription.description: What the index holds, in Markdown. Empty when no description was set. Clients render it without raw HTML.

IndexTags.description: Key/value labels on the index, for example the commit it was synced from. At most 64 tags. A key is 1 to 128 characters without whitespace or control characters; a value is at most 1,024 characters without control characters. Empty when none was set.

IndexTagChanges.description: Tags to set, by key, and tags to remove, given as null. A key absent from the map is unchanged.

TaggedStringMetadataValue.description: A string metadata value with its type named.

TaggedIntegerMetadataValue.description: A 64-bit integer metadata value with its type named.

TaggedNumberMetadataValue.description: A floating-point metadata value with its type named.

value.description: The value, a double-precision floating-point number.

TaggedBooleanMetadataValue.description: A boolean metadata value with its type named.

TaggedTimestampMetadataValue.description: A timestamp metadata value with its type named.

value.description: The value, an RFC 3339 date and time.

MetadataValue.description:
A metadata value: a plain JSON string, boolean or integer, or a tagged value. A number that is not an
integer, and a timestamp, are always tagged. Any value may be tagged. Responses always use the tagged form.

TaggedMetadataValue.description: A metadata value with its type named explicitly.

Metadata.description: Document metadata as a request sends it. Values are plain or tagged.

TaggedMetadata.description: Document metadata as a response returns it. Every value is tagged with its type.

PutDocumentForm.description: One document to store, sent as multipart form fields.

key.description: The document's key: a UTF-8, POSIX-style path of at most 1,024 bytes, with no empty, `.` or `..` components. Storing a key that exists replaces that document.

metadata.description: The document's metadata as a JSON object, at most 64 fields. Optional.

content.description: The document bytes, at most 1 GiB. Valid UTF-8 of at most 100 MiB is searchable; other content is stored without being searchable.

PutObjectRecord.description: One document of a batch to store.

key.description: The document's key: a UTF-8, POSIX-style path of at most 1,024 bytes, with no empty, `.` or `..` components. Storing a key that exists replaces that document.

content.description: The document text. A batch carries text only, so every document it stores is searchable.

metadata.description: The document's metadata, at most 64 fields. Optional.

if_match.description: A revision. The document is stored only if it still has this revision; otherwise its result has the error `precondition_failed`.

if_none_match.description: Set to `*` to store the document only if no document has this key yet; otherwise its result has the error `precondition_failed`.

DeleteObjectRecord.description: One document of a batch to delete.

key.description: The key of the document to delete.

if_match.description: A revision. The document is deleted only if it still has this revision; otherwise its result has the error `precondition_failed`.

MutationResult.description: The outcome of one document. A stored or deleted document has a revision; a document a batch did not change has an error instead.

revision.description: The document's revision after the write. Omitted when the document was not changed.

error.description: Why this document was not changed. Omitted when it was.

MutationBatchResult.description: The outcome of each document of a batch.

results.description: One result per document, in request order.

DocumentSummary.description: A document as a listing returns it, without its content.

revision.description: The document's current revision, an opaque value that changes on every write. Pass it as If-Match to write only if nothing changed since.

content_bytes.description: The size of the document's content, in bytes.

metadata.description: The document's metadata, every value tagged with its type.

updated_at.description: When the document's current revision was stored.

searchable.description: Whether a search can match this document. False for content that is not valid UTF-8 or is over 100 MiB; such a document is stored and served but never returned by a query.

DocumentPage.description: A page of a document listing.

results.description: The documents on this page, in key byte order.

common_prefixes.description: With a delimiter, each distinct key prefix that ends at the delimiter, standing for every document under it. Empty without a delimiter.

pagination.description: How to request the next page.

QueryRequest.description: A search: the pattern, how to match it, which documents to search and how much context to return.

pattern.description: What to search for: an RE2 regular expression, or literal text when `mode` is `literal`. Required; at most 8,192 characters of valid UTF-8.

mode.description: How to read the pattern: `regex` (the default) for RE2 syntax, without backreferences or lookaround, or `literal` to match its bytes exactly, with no escaping needed.

case_sensitive.description: Whether case must match. Defaults to true. False matches under Unicode simple case folding; in a regex, `(?i)` does the same for part of the pattern.

whole_word.description: Match only where the characters on either side of the match aren't word characters: letters, digits or `_`. Defaults to false. Valid only in literal mode.

multiline.description: Let a match span lines. Without it a pattern matches within one line, `^` and `$` mark the line's edges, and a character class never matches a line break; a pattern that contains a line break is rejected. With it the pattern is matched against the whole document, `^` and `$` still mark line edges, `\A` and `\z` mark the document's edges, and a match may contain line breaks.

filter.description: Search only the documents whose metadata matches this expression, such as `path STARTSWITH 'src/' AND size < 1048576`. At most 8,192 characters. Omit it to search every document.

lines_before.description: How many lines before each result to return with it, from the same document.

lines_after.description: How many lines after each result to return with it, from the same document.

Match.description: One match, as a byte range of the document.

offset.description: Byte offset of the match within the document. It starts at byte `offset - text_start_offset` of the result's text.

QueryResult.description: One match, or several matches that share lines, together with the lines it covers. A result covers one line unless the query set multiline and a match spans lines.

key.description: The key of the document that matched.

revision.description: The revision of the document that matched.

line_number.description: One-based number of the first line the result covers.

last_line_number.description: One-based number of the last line the result covers. Equal to line_number unless a match spans lines.

line_start_offset.description: Byte offset of the first covered line's start within the document.

line_end_offset.description: Byte offset just past the last covered line, excluding its line break.

text_start_offset.description: Byte offset of the first byte of text within the document.

text_line_number.description: One-based number of the line text begins on. Equal to line_number unless text was cut at its start.

text.description: The covered lines, up to 64 KiB, centered on the first match when they are longer. Line breaks between covered lines are kept; the last line's break is not.

matches.description: Every match on the covered lines that lies at least partly within text, with byte offsets and lengths relative to the document. A match that consumed the last line's break extends one byte past text.

text_truncated.description: Whether text was cut at either end.

matches_truncated.description: Whether matches were left out, because there were more than 4096 or because they lie outside text.

lines_before.description: The requested lines before the result, in document order, ending at the line just above its first line. Fewer are returned at the start of the document, and the field is omitted when there are none.

lines_after.description: The requested lines after the result, in document order, starting at the line just below its last line. Fewer are returned at the end of the document, and the field is omitted when there are none.

ContextLine.description: One line near a result. Text is returned whole up to 64 KiB, and up to 64 KiB away from the result; a line that extends past either bound is returned in part and marked truncated.

text.description: The line's text, without its line break, up to 64 KiB.

results.description: The results on this page, sorted by key, then line, then offset.

pagination.description: How to request the next page.
